target: C'est à côté du supermarché.
english: It's next to the supermarket.
tip: 'À côté de' means next to, and 'de + le' contracts to 'du': 'à côté du supermarché', never 'de le supermarché'.

target: Tu as payé l'addition ?
english: Did you pay the bill?
tip: L'addition is the restaurant bill, not a math sum: tu as payé l'addition = did you pay the bill?

target: Soixante, soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix, cent.
english: Sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, one hundred.
tip: 70 = soixante-dix (60+10), 80 = quatre-vingts (4×20), 90 = quatre-vingt-dix (4×20+10). Unique to French counting.

target: Vingt et un, trente, quarante, cinquante.
english: Twenty-one, thirty, forty, fifty.
tip: 21 and its cousins take a bare 'et', no hyphens: 'vingt et un', trente et un. But most compounds just hyphenate: vingt-deux, trente-trois.

target: J'ai fini de manger à midi.
english: I finished eating at noon.
tip: Finir attaches to the next verb with de: j'ai fini de manger = I finished eating. Different verbs pick à or de – finir takes de.

target: Elle est fière de son travail.
english: She is proud of her work.
tip: The feminine adds a grave accent: masculine 'fier' becomes 'fière', the same spelling shift as premier/première.

target: Il est sorti acheter du pain.
english: He went out to buy bread.
tip: Sortir uses être, not avoir, in the past: 'il est sorti' = he went out. Never 'il a sorti' for going out.

target: Tu as regardé le film hier ?
english: Did you watch the movie yesterday?
tip: Regarder already means 'look at,' so no preposition follows: tu as regardé le film = you watched the film, never regardé à.

target: Nous sommes restés à l'hôtel ce jour-là.
english: We stayed at the hotel that day.
tip: Rester takes être even though nobody moves: 'nous sommes restés' = we stayed. Staying put still counts as an être verb.

target: J'ai attendu le train pendant trente minutes.
english: I waited for the train for thirty minutes.
tip: Attendre swallows the 'for': j'ai attendu le train = I waited for the train. Adding pour here would be wrong.

target: Tu as cuisiné quelque chose de bon ?
english: Did you cook something good?
tip: After quelque chose, French links the adjective with de and keeps it masculine: quelque chose de bon = something good.

target: Bravo, tu as réussi ton examen avec brio!
english: Well done, you passed your exam brilliantly!
tip: You don't 'pass' an exam in French, you succeed at it: tu as réussi ton examen = you passed your exam.

target: Écoute, je dois te dire quelque chose d'important.
english: Listen, I need to tell you something important.
tip: 'Écoute' is the informal imperative (tu form) of 'écouter'. Used as an interjection to get attention.

target: Elle cuisinait toujours un bon repas le dimanche.
english: She always cooked a good meal on Sundays.
tip: 'Le dimanche' with the article means 'on Sundays' as a habit, not one specific Sunday. Drop the 'le' and it's just this coming Sunday.

target: Regarde le beau coucher de soleil sur la mer.
english: Look at the beautiful sunset over the sea.
tip: The tu command drops the -s: you write 'tu regardes' but 'Regarde !' when telling someone to look.

target: Elle a ouvert un livre et a commencé à lire.
english: She opened a book and started reading.
tip: Commencer links to the next verb with à: a commencé à lire = started to read. The à is required before the infinitive.

target: Tu savais que le magasin fermait a dix-huit heures ?
english: Did you know the store closed at six PM?
tip: France runs on a 24-hour clock: 'dix-huit heures' (eighteen hours) is 6 PM. Add 12 to any afternoon time to get the everyday form.

target: Il porte une barbe.
english: He has a beard.
tip: 'Porter une barbe' = to wear/have a beard. French uses 'porter' (to wear) for facial hair.

target: Peut-être devrions-nous changer notre approche.
english: Maybe we should change our approach.
tip: Start a sentence with 'peut-être' and the verb jumps ahead of the subject: 'devrions-nous'. To skip the inversion, say 'peut-être qu'on...' instead.

target: Je me lève à sept heures.
english: I get up at seven o'clock.
tip: French literally says 'I raise myself': 'je me lève' = I get up. Drop the 'me' and 'je lève' just means I lift something else.

target: J'ai mangé au restaurant hier soir.
english: I ate at the restaurant last night.
tip: 'à + le' must merge into 'au': you can't say 'à le restaurant', only 'au restaurant'.

target: Tu as acheté un billet aller-retour ?
english: Did you buy a round-trip ticket?
tip: In questions, the structure stays the same: tu as + past participle. Intonation rises.

target: Nous avons passé deux semaines en Espagne.
english: We spent two weeks in Spain.
tip: Feminine countries take en for 'in' or 'to': en Espagne = in Spain. No article – it's not 'dans l'Espagne.'

target: J'ai réservé deux places pour le concert.
english: I reserved two seats for the concert.
tip: Une place is a seat or spot here, not just a 'place': deux places pour le concert = two seats for the concert.

target: Nous avons commandé des pizzas pour le dîner.
english: We ordered pizzas for dinner.
tip: Commander means to order food, not to command: nous avons commandé des pizzas = we ordered pizzas.

target: Il est entré dans la pièce sans frapper.
english: He entered the room without knocking.
tip: Entrer needs dans before a place: il est entré dans la pièce = he entered the room. And it takes être, not avoir, in the past.

target: Il a téléphoné à son frère en Allemagne.
english: He called his brother in Germany.
tip: Téléphoner needs à before the person: il a téléphoné à son frère = he called his brother. You phone 'to' someone in French.

target: Nous avons fermé le magasin à vingt heures.
english: We closed the store at eight PM.
tip: France runs on the 24-hour clock: vingt heures is 8 PM, literally 'twenty hours.' Vingt et une heures would be 9 PM.

target: Il a cherché ses clés pendant une heure.
english: He looked for his keys for an hour.
tip: Chercher already contains the 'for': il a cherché ses clés = he looked for his keys. Never add pour after it.

target: Tu savais déjà parler anglais à dix ans ?
english: Did you already know how to speak English at ten?
tip: 'Déjà' + imparfait describes a state that was already true: 'tu savais déjà' = you already knew.
